maya.blurb: Conversational and kind. Draws out your story with gentle follow-ups. No tricks.
maya.style: Calm pace · open questions · listens back · encouraging · never combative
maya.company: Talent partner at a fast-growing company

june.blurb: Cares about the mission. Wants to know why this company and why now.
june.style: Friendly and quick · asks about motivation first · tests how sincere the answer is
june.company: Founder and CEO of an early-stage company

nova.blurb: Curious and fast. Moves across the whole field and asks what else is out there.
nova.style: Wide-ranging · compares alternatives · aware of trends · moves sideways rather than deeper
nova.company: Principal at a global consulting firm

priya.blurb: Asks about real past situations until your answer has a clear action and a clear result.
priya.style: Story-based · situation, action, result · patient follow-ups · conflict and failure · separates what you did from what the team did
priya.company: People lead at a large consumer brand

rex.blurb: Hands you a problem you have not seen and watches how you break it down.
rex.style: Open problems · estimates and hypotheticals · reason out loud · changes one constraint mid-answer

diaz.blurb: Calm manager who has done the job. Keeps asking what you specifically did.
diaz.style: Even-tempered · practice over theory · one real example, step by step

atlas.blurb: Senior generalist. Maps what you know and asks about the parts you skip.
atlas.style: Breadth first · across areas · finds the gaps by moving to the next area
atlas.company: Distinguished engineer at a large tech company

bishop.blurb: Wants the failure, the disagreement you lost, and proof you owned it.
bishop.style: Ownership · asks for failure and conflict · distrusts rehearsed answers · what did you do
bishop.company: Hiring director at a fast-growing company

okonkwo.blurb: Rigorous, and keeps changing the problem. Cares how you think under pressure.
okonkwo.style: First principles · structured breakdown · tightening constraints · questions your assumptions
okonkwo.company: Partner at a top strategy firm

kai.blurb: Digs three levels down. Wants the exact decision and the case where it broke.
kai.style: Technical depth · quiet pauses · walk me through exactly what happened
kai.company: Senior staff engineer on a large infrastructure team

voss.blurb: Pushes back on every claim. Wants the number behind the story.
voss.style: Pointed · skeptical · numbers first · how do you know that

lena.blurb: Cares how clearly you land the point. Will ask you to explain the hard thing simply.
lena.style: Audience first · explain it to someone new · rewards a clean opening line · catches rambling
lena.company: Communications lead who has coached hundreds of executives

mirae.blurb: Changes topic every two minutes and keeps the clock running.
mirae.style: Fast topic changes · timed answers · high tempo · rewards adapting quickly
mirae.company: Final-round panel chair at a large tech company

osei.blurb: Looks at how you treat people when it is hard. Asks about putting the team first.
osei.style: Values in action · collaboration stories · how did the team feel · warm but probing
osei.company: Head of people at a values-driven company

devi.blurb: Hands you an open problem and works it with you. Cares how you frame it.
devi.style: Reasoning together · nudges your framing · thinking matters more than the answer
devi.company: Product strategist who reasons out loud with you

amara.blurb: Moves across markets and fields, looking for range and the links you can draw.
amara.style: Across industries · maps the market · who else does this well · connects ideas

sterling.blurb: Senior, exacting, unhurried. Wants the short version first, then the proof.
sterling.style: Formal · headline first · concise under questioning · tests precision
sterling.company: Board-level operator at a large company

tariq.blurb: Pushes hard and fast, talks over you, turns your answer back on you.
tariq.style: Rapid questions · interrupts and challenges · argues the other side · tests composure

security.metaDescription: How %BRAND% protects your account and data, in plain words.
security.title: Security
security.lead: What we actually do to protect your account and your data. If something here changes, this page changes with it.
security.account1: Passwords are stored only as salted one-way hashes. We can't read your password.
security.account2: Sign-in cookies can't be read by scripts on the page and travel only over encrypted connections.
security.account3: When your account signs in from a new browser or device, we email you.
security.account4: Sign-in attempts and other sensitive actions are rate-limited.
security.data1: You can download a copy of your data and delete your account from Settings.
security.data2: We never send an application, message or form to an employer for you.
security.data3: There are no third-party advertising pixels or trackers on %BRAND%.
security.aiIntl: Your resume and job data go only to the AI providers named in the privacy policy. They are never sent to AI services in mainland China.
security.aiCn: AI processing starts only after you turn it on, and you can turn it off at any time. Where data is processed and stored is stated in the privacy policy.
security.aiSensitive: Sensitive details such as a photo, birth date, gender or family members are never sent to an AI model.

help.sub: Answers to common questions. Can't find yours? Write to us below.

q1.q: How do I reset my password?
q1.a: On the sign-in page, choose Forgot password and follow the email we send.

q2.q: How do I cancel a subscription?
q2.a: In Settings under Billing, or without signing in on the cancel page. Access continues until the end of the period you paid for.

q3.q: Why did a job disappear from my list?
q3.a: It may have closed, been removed by its source, or been hidden by a filter you set. Closed jobs show when they were last seen.

q4.q: I opened an application but didn't apply. How do I fix it?
q4.a: Use Undo on the job, or change its status on your applications board.

q5.q: How do I delete my account?
q5.a: In Settings, under the account section. You can download a copy of your data first.

q6.q: Why does the fit score say it isn't my chance of getting hired?
q6.a: Because it only measures how well your resume lines up with the post. Hiring depends on many things we can't see.

ranking.lead: The For you list (sort: Recommended) is ordered by four factors. Here is each one, with its weight.

fit.title: Fit to your resume and search
fit.body: Your fit score for the job, out of 100. When a full fit analysis isn't available yet, a quick estimate is used, counted slightly lower.

freshness.title: Freshness
freshness.body: Newer posts come first. The effect fades over about three days.

affinity.title: What you've shown interest in
affinity.body: Jobs like the ones you saved or opened move up; jobs like the ones you hid move down. Older actions count for less.

source.title: Listing source

skillsBoost.title: Your chosen skills
skillsBoost.body: When skills are the only filter narrowing your list, jobs that ask for more of your chosen skills rank higher in Recommended, in proportion to how many of them the job asks for.

layout_table.title: Table in your resume
layout_table.why: Company software may not read this. Tables often come out scrambled when hiring software reads a resume.
layout_table.how: Turn the table into plain lines or bullets.

layout_columns.title: Two-column layout
layout_columns.why: Company software may not read this. It can read across both columns and mix lines together.

layout_image.title: Image in your resume
layout_image.why: Company software may not read this. Text inside images, icons or charts cannot be read.
layout_image.how: Remove images and write the information as text.

layout_symbols.title: Symbols or emoji ({symbol})
layout_symbols.why: Company software may not read this. Emoji and decorative symbols can turn into odd characters.
layout_symbols.how: Replace symbols with plain words, for example "Email:" instead of an icon.

contact_name_missing.title: No name at the top
contact_name_missing.why: Without a name at the top, nobody knows whose resume this is.
contact_name_missing.how: Put your full name on the first line.

contact_email_missing.title: No email address
contact_email_missing.why: Employers need a way to reply to you.
contact_email_missing.how: Add an email address you check every day.

contact_phone_missing.title: No phone number
contact_phone_missing.why: Many employers call to set up the first conversation.

section_experience_missing.title: No experience section
section_experience_missing.why: Experience is the first thing most readers look for.
section_experience_missing.how: Add an Experience section with your jobs, internships or substantial projects.

section_education_missing.title: No education section
section_education_missing.why: Many postings list an education requirement, and readers check for it.
section_education_missing.how: Add an Education section with school, degree and dates.

section_skills_missing.title: No skills section
section_skills_missing.why: A skills list is where readers and software look for the tools a job asks for.
section_skills_missing.how: Add a Skills section with the tools and methods you actually use.

summary_missing.title: No summary
summary_missing.why: Two sentences at the top tell the reader what you do before they read the details.
summary_missing.how: Add a short summary: your role, your strongest area, and what you want next.

summary_too_short.title: Very short summary
summary_too_short.why: A very short summary does not say what makes you a fit.
summary_too_short.how: Write two or three sentences about your role, your strongest area and a result.

summary_too_long.title: Long summary
summary_too_long.why: Readers skim the top of a resume; a long summary gets skipped.
summary_too_long.how: Cut it to two or three sentences.

weak_verb.title: Weak opener: "{opener}"
weak_verb.why: Openers like "responsible for" describe a duty, not what you did.
weak_verb.how: Start with what you did: built, led, cut, shipped.

no_numbers.title: Few results with numbers ({withNumbers} of {total} bullets)
no_numbers.why: Few of your bullets show a result someone could measure.
no_numbers.how: Add a real number where you have one: people, time, money, volume or percent. Do not guess.

bullet_too_long.title: Long bullet
bullet_too_long.why: Long bullets are hard to skim.
bullet_too_long.how: Keep each bullet to one or two lines: what you did and the result.

buzzwords.title: Common phrases: {terms}
buzzwords.why: Phrases every resume uses do not tell the reader anything about you.
buzzwords.how: Replace them with a specific example of the quality you mean.

skills_too_few.title: Short skills list ({count} listed)
skills_too_few.why: A short skills list can hide tools a job asks for.
skills_too_few.how: List the tools, languages and methods you use, at least {min}.

length_too_long.title: Longer than two pages
length_too_long.why: This resume is likely longer than two pages, and readers rarely get that far.
length_too_long.how: Keep it to one or two pages: cut older or less relevant bullets.

spelling.title: Possible spelling mistake: "{word}"
spelling.why: Spelling mistakes are noticed quickly and look careless.

summary_vague.title: General summary
summary_vague.why: The summary is general and could describe many people.
summary_vague.how: Name your role, your strongest area and one real result.

cn_self_evaluation_missing.title: No self-evaluation (自我评价)
cn_self_evaluation_missing.why: Many Chinese employers expect a short self-evaluation.
cn_self_evaluation_missing.how: Add two or three sentences with concrete strengths, not slogans.

cn_internship_missing.title: No internship (实习)
cn_internship_missing.why: For students and new graduates, internships are the experience employers look for first.
cn_internship_missing.how: Add an internship section, or list substantial projects or campus work if you have no internship.

cn_english_cert_missing.title: No English certificate listed
cn_english_cert_missing.why: Many employers check English level (CET-4/6, IELTS, TOEFL).
cn_english_cert_missing.how: If you have an English certificate or score, list it under skills and certificates.

cn_personal_details_optional.title: Optional personal details ({label})
cn_personal_details_optional.why: Details like 籍贯, 政治面貌 or birth date are optional on most resumes.
cn_personal_details_optional.how: Keep them only if the employer asks for them.

cn_photo_optional.title: Photo (optional)
cn_photo_optional.why: A photo is optional. Some employers ask for one; many do not.
cn_photo_optional.how: Keep a recent, professional photo only if the employer asks for one.
